walkthroughs.h2: How Do We Know Black Holes Exist?
walkthroughs.body_html: We cannot see black holes directly but infer them from: orbits of stars near invisible massive objects, X-rays from accretion discs, jets from active galaxies, and direct images from the Event Horizon Telescope.
A supermassive black hole eating gas produces a hot accretion disc that outshines its host galaxy. Quasars are the most luminous AGN, visible across the observable universe.
When asked 'how can a black hole be detected', mention indirect evidence: stellar orbits at the galactic centre, X-ray binaries, gravitational waves and the EHT image of M87 (2019).
